suggestion: Retire the six older site trees and keep this dashboard as the single live surface
why: Seven trees carry the same subjects with different numbers and incompatible ID namespaces. A reviewer cannot tell which figure is current without reading the coordination log.
options: A - keep all seven and mark them 'archived' at the top of each page; B - keep /origin/ (the engine) plus this dashboard and delete the rest; C - keep only this dashboard
impact: High - removes the risk of acting on a stale number.

suggestion: Add a single 'eligible to act' flag at the top of every pick row
why: Every pick currently carries its own strategy status string in prose. One machine-readable flag makes the leaderboard and the picks consistent.
options: A - one flag with the gate list that failed; B - three states (eligible, provisional, not eligible)
impact: High - removes ambiguity in the picks table.

suggestion: Publish the gate score and the power calculation for every strategy, not just a pass or fail
why: S5 and S4b fail only on sample size. Showing the power curve tells a reviewer whether to wait or to abandon a strategy.
options: A - power curve per strategy; B - the number of extra games needed at the current effect size
impact: Medium - turns a null result into a decision.

suggestion: Capture per-player game logs for two seasons
why: Player-level correlation is the missing input for player-prop parlays and for any real injury-to-minutes impact. Four correlation cells are blank because of it.
options: A - nba.com/stats player box scores; B - skip player props entirely and remove those pages
impact: High - unlocks the whole player-prop branch.

suggestion: Re-source the game results from nba.com box scores
why: Results currently come from Basketball-Reference. The aggregate check reconciles exactly, but a per-game check against official box scores is stronger.
options: A - replace the results log with nba.com box scores; B - keep Basketball-Reference and keep the provenance note
impact: Medium - makes every model input official.

suggestion: Derive the three-day window from the official schedule instead of hard coding it
why: The current generator only knows 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16, so it will produce an empty or wrong slate tomorrow.
options: A - read nba.com/schedule at run time; B - read the official schedule PDF; C - keep it manual but document the update step
impact: High - the system becomes usable on an ongoing basis.

suggestion: Run a scheduled check that every published number still matches its source
why: Official statistics move during the season, and an injury report is replaced eight times a day. Numbers on a static site decay silently.
options: A - a daily job that re-fetches and diffs; B - a printed retrieval timestamp on every table (already partly done)
impact: Medium - stops the site from quietly going stale.

suggestion: Add a 'last updated' banner and a per-table retrieval stamp
why: A reader cannot tell whether a number was published today or three weeks ago.
options: A - banner only; B - banner plus a stamp on every table

suggestion: Add a filter box to the picks and injuries tables
why: Both tables are long and the useful view is usually one date or one team.
options: A - plain client-side filter with no framework; B - one filter per column

suggestion: Add a bankroll and staking panel next to the leaderboard
why: A leaderboard without a stake rule invites the reader to size bets by confidence rather than by risk.
options: A - flat 1 unit per bet with a stated bankroll; B - fractional Kelly with a published cap
impact: Medium - prevents the most common misuse of a leaderboard.

suggestion: Clean up the repository: add a licence, drop the unused requests pin, and move the one-shot generators out of the build path
why: scripts/archive/ holds generators that overwrite data/ if run again, and requirements.txt lists a library nothing imports.
options: A - delete both; B - keep them but rename to tools/ and mark them clearly

suggestion: Decide whether the older market-price picks page stays public
why: It publishes positive-EV labels against a third-party odds feed under a pre-validation tier, with the licensing flags above still open.
options: A - take it down; B - keep it but relabel it 'research only, not a recommendation'
